messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: model-init failures detected on cluster us-west-2-prd-4. Error spike on /v1/generate routes for model 'open-llama-13b-v1' — 5xx rate up 18% in last 2m. Auto-mitigation attempted: retry, fallback-policy none.

sara: taking ownership — I'm oncall. quick status? any customer-impact signals?

mike: seeing repeated failures during warmup on a subset of GPUs. logs show OOM while mapping tensors and occasional CUDA driver errors. tail from one failed pod:

```
E tensorflow: failed to allocate 24.3 GiB (allocator: cuda_malloc)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "loader.py", line 214, in load_model
    state = torch.load(f, map_location='cpu')
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 789, in load
    return _load(f, map_location, pickle_module, **kwargs)
_pickle.UnpicklingError: invalid load key, '\x00'
RuntimeError: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_STATE: unknown error
```

jess: confirmed: node p-4-21 shows repeated container restarts and OOM kills. kube events show eviction + restart loop.

raja: also seeing a few compile-timeouts coming from the XLA/torchscript compile step: `compile_timeout=30s` expired. it's possible the combined compile + deserialization spikes memory.

emma: support notes — customers A and B reported 503s starting ~13:14 UTC. Affected region: us-west-2. Priority customer flagged.

sara: immediate plan: 1) reduce incoming traffic to problematic node pool, 2) route to fallback model variant (smaller / quantized), 3) attempt graceful pod drain + restart on nodes with driver errors.

mike: executing drain on node p-4-21 now: `kubectl drain p-4-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ops-bot: WARN: draining node p-4-21 will evict 42 pods. Pod disruption budget for service/model-route allows 1 unavailable.

jess: scaling up dedicated pool by +2 instances to absorb traffic: `redwood infra scale --pool prd-gpu-rt --delta 2 --region us-west-2` — ETA 90s.

raja: preparing a quick model fallback: v1 -> v1-q4_8 (quantized) which reduces memory by ~55%. I can push route override for region us-west-2.

mike: quick check — any persistent NV driver crashes? `dmesg` on node shows: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:82:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus`. That's a flaky card; we'll mark for replace later. For now draining is correct.

emma: posting a customer update draft: "We're investigating elevated errors for text-generation in US-West. We've applied a regional fallback to a lower-memory model to reduce impact; you may see slightly different latency/quality. We'll follow up with a full remediation timeline." Thoughts?

sara: looks good, send now and include contact info. set severity P1 for tracking because of a paying customer.

mike: fallback route applied: `redwood route set --model open-llama-13b-v1-q4_8 --region us-west-2 --force` — confirmed traffic shift ~2m ago. error rate for /v1/generate down to baseline for most customers.

ops-bot: METRIC: 5xx-rate (/v1/generate, us-west-2) dropped from 18% -> 2.1% within 3m of routing change. Latency percentile p95 up ~120ms due to smaller model CPU/latency tradeoff.

jess: node p-4-21 restarted by kubelet but shows repeated driver faults; isolating it from scheduling: `kubectl cordon p-4-21` and filed HW ticket with cloud provider (ticket 87654321).

raja: follow-up: I kicked off a quick artifact re-validation for the model tarball — saw a corrupted chunk in the object store for one shard which may explain the pickle/deser errors. checksum mismatch for shard-12. open a ticket to re-ingest artifact from canonical source.

mike: compile-timeouts — increased compile timeout to 90s temporarily for warmup jobs to reduce spurious failures: updated config: `MODEL_COMPILE_TIMEOUT=90s` for warmup controller. We'll monitor for any slow lockups.

emma: customer update posted and sent to A + B. they acknowledged. no escalations so far.

sara: current status summary: - Impact: customers in us-west-2 saw 503s for ~12m window. - Mitigation: regional route fallback to quantized model applied; node drained & cordoned; pool scaled +2. - Root cause likely: combination of corrupted model shard causing deserialization errors + flaky GPU driver causing OOM and compile timeouts during warmup.

jess: can someone own postmortem and timeline? I'll own infra remediation (node replacement + PDB tuning).

sara: I'll own postmortem and coord with ML infra for artifact re-ingest. action items: sara (postmortem), raja (artifact re-ingest + validation), jess (node replacement + review PDB), mike (warmup timeout tuning rollback), emma (customer follow-up).

raja: immediate next step — reupload clean shard-12 to object store and invalidate CDN/cache for model artifacts in us-west-2. Will do and report when available.

mike: monitoring: enabling extra tracing for deserializers for next 24h: `LOG_LEVEL=debug deserializer=trace`.

ops-bot: NOTE: incident auto-archiver disabled for this thread.

emma: customers ask ETA for when full-quality model will return — suggest: "we aim to restore the full model in 2-4 hours after artifact re-ingest and warmup validation." ok with everyone?

sara: ok. locking timeline to 4h max. we'll update if it changes. closing notes: we avoided broad customer impact by fallback; we need better artifact validation and early checksum verification during deploy to prevent deser-caused init failures.

jess: adding retrospective item: consider using staging warmup for every artifact change or add per-shard checksum gating.

sara: thanks all — handing off to night oncall at 00:00 UTC, @mike please monitor the tracing alerts and @raja keep me posted on artifact re-ingest.

mike: ack.

raja: ack, uploading shard now (upload id 0x9c4f). will report success.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE (5423456789): mitigated -> partial; severity -> P1; owner -> sara; postmortem-owner -> sara.
